title: 2026-12-28 Zenith - Postmortem & Mitigation Follow-up
meeting_header: 2026-12-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: 57m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Natarajan, Daniel Park (Redwood) / Maria Gonzalez, Thomas Lee, Nora Patel, Evan Brooks (Zenith)
summary: Follow-up to the 2026-12-20 incident: reviewed root cause (KV cache eviction + autoscaler interaction), confirmed short-term mitigations, outlined medium-term reliability improvements and security clarifications. Agreed on deliverables: logs/benchmarks, patch timeline, and a pilot run on Dedicated capacity for critical routes.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through the postmortem and the mitigation plan. Maria, do you want to kick off with how it impacted you from a customer side?
[00:18] Maria Gonzalez: Yeah thanks Alex. We saw increased p99 latencies around 13:12 UTC on the 20th, timeouts in our user-facing flows, and a handful of failed writes to our audit pipeline. It lasted roughly 18 minutes before the fallback started working.
[00:36] Thomas Lee: To add, the incident caused downstream queue buildup, Jenkins jobs timed out, so the blast radius touched a couple internal services.
[00:49] Priya Natarajan: Sorry just to confirm - that aligns with the logs we shared where we saw heavy KV cache eviction and then traffic sheddin' behavior as pods spun up. It looked like the autoscaler interacted with cache warmup in a way that spiked latencies.
[01:05] Nora Patel: From a security perspective we flagged the audit logs gap, we need confirmation those events are durably stored and will be forwarded.
[01:20] Alex Chen: Understood. Quick reminder: this call is to agree on mitigations, timeline and any follow-ups for your SOC/compliance team.
[01:35] Priya Natarajan: Root cause summary from our side: small-model serving pods evicted KV caches when they were scaled down. When traffic spiked we scaled up new pods but cache warmup latency plus request queuing caused token-level latencies to jump. The autoscaler threshold settings caused rapid scale events which amplified the problem. Also there was a config mismatch between cache retention on Dedicated-vs-hosted routes — some of the routes were on a relaxed TTL that wasn't suitable for transient spikes.
[02:10] Maria Gonzalez: Is that the KV cache or the K V cache? Some of our folks misread the logs.
[02:16] Priya Natarajan: It's KV cache, like key-value for prefix/kvcache. The transcription sometimes says K V cache in our notes.
[02:25] Evan Brooks: Can you explain briefly why Dedicated would behave differently? We were surprised because we had pinned capacity.
[02:32] Daniel Park: Sure — for pinned Dedicated pools we still rely on cache retention config. If application-level routing had a mix of model variants (small quantized vs full), requests could be routed to cheaper variants under certain policies. That contributed to cold-start patterns for some of your routes.
[02:55] Thomas Lee: Okay. So immediate questions: what can be done now to prevent recurrence in the short term?
[03:05] Alex Chen: Short term fixes we agreed on: 1) increase KV cache retention on critical routes to avoid eviction during transient scale-downs; 2) temporarily raise autoscaler cooldowns and tighten thresholds to avoid rapid scale churn; 3) enable request-level circuit breaker for the user-facing path so requests route to a warmed fallback model instead of queuing; 4) replay logs to validate no data loss for audit events.
[03:40] Maria Gonzalez: Timeline?
[03:45] Alex Chen: We can push a config change to increase retention today for the critical routes; Priya will coordinate and we can roll the autoscaler change by tomorrow EOD. The circuit breaker toggle is a small runtime flag we can late-stage flip and test in staging today, then roll to prod in a canary.
[04:05] Priya Natarajan: I'll also send an updated rollout playbook — includes smoke tests and rollback steps.
[04:12] Nora Patel: On the audit logs, do you still have the missing events? We need guarantees about durability and encryption at rest — KMS integration.
[04:20] Alex Chen: We do have the events; some were delayed. We will provide the delivery logs and hashes. Regarding KMS, for Private and Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for encryption at rest; I can share the integration docs.
[04:40] Evan Brooks: Another ask — can Redwood provide a short postmortem doc we can attach to our internal RCA?
[04:46] Daniel Park: Yes, we'll update the postmortem and include a clear timeline, root cause, mitigation steps, and the monitoring/alerts we changed.
[04:55] Maria Gonzalez: We also want SLO adjustments and an SLA credit discussion if this meets the threshold.
[05:02] Alex Chen: Understood, we'll surface it to the account team and legal; Daniel will own the SLA credit review.
[05:10] Priya Natarajan: Longer-term reliability improvements discussed: adaptive cache sizing, smarter warming (background prefetch for hot prefixes), improved autoscaler heuristics aware of cache warmup, per-route canarying, and better tracing to see hop-by-hop token latency.
[05:34] Thomas Lee: For the autoscaler heuristics, do you have a timeline? We need a roadmap to present to execs.
[05:40] Priya Natarajan: Medium-term roadmap: engineering intends to ship autoscaler heuristics and warmup-aware scaling in Q1 2027; background prefetch and adaptive sizing targeted Q2 2027. We'll give you a tracked engineering ticket.
[05:55] Maria Gonzalez: Any immediate mitigations we can test on our side? We're open to a pilot where we run critical routes on Dedicated pinned capacity.
[06:03] Alex Chen: We recommend a Dedicated pilot for your top 10 routes — we can provision Reserved capacity with stricter retention and no aggressive cost-saving routing. That would remove routing-induced cold starts.
[06:20] Evan Brooks: Pricing and lead time?
[06:24] Alex Chen: We'll send a draft pricing proposal; provisioning can be done in 5-7 business days once contracts are signed.
[06:35] Nora Patel: A few security checklist items: SOC 2 attestation, ISO, SAML SSO logs, role-based access, audit log retention policy. We'll need docs.
[06:47] Daniel Park: We'll share the security pack and the SOC/ISO artifacts. For SAML and RBAC we have recommended patterns and screenshots.
[06:58] Maria Gonzalez: When you say "security pack", can you include the exact log fields that will be present when we enable the forwarding? We need to map to our SIEM.
[07:06] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll provide the log schema and sample events.
[07:10] Thomas Lee: Let's talk about monitoring: can you add a custom alert when KV cache eviction rate goes above X per minute? That's what would have caught this earlier.
[07:20] Priya Natarajan: Absolutely — we can add eviction-rate alerts and increase histogram resolution for p50/p95/p99 token latencies. We'll also add a synthetic check for the critical user path.
[07:36] Maria Gonzalez: Great. Any concerns about data residency during the Dedicated pilot?
[07:42] Alex Chen: Dedicated can be pinned to a region; for Private deployments we can support VPC/on-prem if you need full data residency. We'll note the region requirements in the provisioning doc.
[07:55] Evan Brooks: A couple of smaller items flagged by our legal team: we need confirmation on log retention durations and deletion APIs.
[08:03] Daniel Park: We'll include the log retention policy and API docs.
[08:10] Maria Gonzalez: Ok let's recap next steps then.
[08:14] Alex Chen: Quick recap: Redwood to increase KV cache retention on critical routes today, flip autoscaler cooldowns by tomorrow EOD, enable circuit breaker canary today, provide logs and sample events, send Dedicated pilot pricing and provisioning timeline, and update postmortem doc.
[08:33] Priya Natarajan: I'll also provide an engineering ticket for the autoscaler heuristic roadmap and target dates.
[08:40] Thomas Lee: For the logs: please include the raw token-level latency traces and the pod lifecycle events so we can map pod spin-up to the latency spike.
[08:50] Alex Chen: Noted. We'll include flamegraphs and the per-request traces.
[08:55] Evan Brooks: Can we schedule a follow-up in one week to validate mitigation results?
[09:00] Alex Chen: Yes, propose same time next week, I'll send calendar invite.
[09:06] Maria Gonzalez: Thanks everyone.
[09:10] [long silence and background chatter 09:10-15:00]
[15:12] Priya Natarajan: (screen share) here's the playbook snippet, note the smoke test steps.
[15:28] Maria Gonzalez: Looks good, minor ask to add the SIEM mapping in step 3.
[20:00] Daniel Park: A few side notes: we saw another transient 503 earlier this month during a network maintenance window — unrelated but we will include it in the incident appendix.
[30:15] Alex Chen: Any final questions about the SLA credit process?
[30:22] Maria Gonzalez: We'll send the internal threshold doc, then we can reconcile.
[40:05] Priya Natarajan: Closing notes on reliability: we'll instrument a new metric called cache_warmup_time and alert at 95th > 500ms.
[45:00] Nora Patel: Security will follow up for a technical review of KMS integration.
[50:20] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone — action items will be in the follow-up email, and Daniel will update the postmortem.
[56:50] Alex Chen: Meeting adjourned.
